items.reason: vectors.py gap. A.0.4 and the M0 exit require that vectors.py assert no floats. json.dumps serialises tuples as arrays, but the assertion skipped them, so a tuple-held float would have been hashed unchecked. The docstring's json.dumps(sort_keys) = RFC 8785 equivalence needs ASCII keys (JCS sorts by UTF-16 code units), and nothing asserted that. No current hashed value had either form: no printed value changes and vectors.json is byte-identical.

items.reading: A.12.6 RJ14 ('an effect fact without n from a presence-sound observer'); A.5.2.1; A.12.5.2; A.12.8.4; RECORDS §2 and §3 (Example 1's fact carries n: 1); RFC D15. A.5.2.13: rejected records do not count as supplied, so the unfixed input would also have raised E-provider-missing.

A.3.4.5 defines the lift to Undeclared<Trust> only for registry kinds. Syntax §4 std declares every kind A.12.2.8 lists (11 kinds; Example 2 counts twelve forbids), so a std-importing shape cannot leave a registry 1.0 kind undeclared, and imports are all-or-nothing (syntax §2 File ::= … ('import' QName)*). A.3.4.4 and A.12.2.8 say what a conforming builder counts, A.12.7.5 lists the conditions that make a manifest invalid and does not include unknown marker kinds, and A.10.1 E-unknown covers shape text only. The text therefore does not decide a non-registry marker. RFC D1 makes Undeclared a fail-closed catch-all, and with std 1.0 that clause can only ever see kinds std does not declare, for example kinds a later registry adds. Lifting to Undeclared<Trust> is the reading most consistent with D1.
items.annex_wording: A.3.4.5 (add): "A manifest marker whose kind the shape does not declare for the identity's language, including a kind outside the checker's registry version, lifts to Undeclared<Trust>; it is never dropped and never makes the manifest invalid. With std 1.0 and registry 1.0 every registry kind is declared, so the Undeclared clause sees only such kinds. Vector: a ts marker of a kind std does not declare, inside a boundary allowing ts_ignore, raises one sound contradiction against effect.forbid(Undeclared<std::Trust>, [*], [])."

items.item: input:all vectors-A (shape.source.v1 stand-in instead of RECORDS §4 files/commit/packs/trustRoots; unsigned bare manifests)
items.reading: RECORDS §4 and A.12.7.1 define the input as files [{path, text}] plus commit, packs and trustRoots, and the vectors-A inputs do not conform to that. The same stand-in is used by spec/example-inputs, by m0/golden/inputs, and by m0/vectors/check.ts, whose kernel route requires head.source (FORMAT.md). Unsigned manifests are allowed when the base names no manifest identity (A.5.2.17: health lists them as unauthenticated). Rewriting 27 vectors here would split them from the golden set and the runner. This is a programme-level deviation that M0 sign-off has to accept, or that M1 has to cover with a converter. It is not a defect of these vectors.
items.annex_wording: Not annex: add to m0/vectors/FORMAT.md: "Inputs use the prototype's shape.source.v1 stand-in (head/base.source, no commit, packs or trustRoots). A version 7 checker is run on them through the stand-in reader, or through a converter to RECORDS §4 files that M1 supplies; the stand-in carries no meaning beyond records §4."

items.item: input:claim judgments supplied in records (barrel-import, guard-helper-edit, preview-equals-change, approve-without-exception, allowed-hatch-at-boundary)
items.reading: No RJ rule rejects a judgment in records, and RJ11 restricts only persisted records. RJ07 names an 'unsigned judgment' separately from a 'persisted record'. A.6.3.3 refers to judgments 'that the relay produced in this run'. A.5.3.5 and A.5.4 do not depend on persistence. D28 and A.7.6.8 concern review lines without a relay, which make no judgment. Neither D28's 'always a persisted record' nor A.7.6.3's 'committed as conforming record files' says whether phase 2 reads those files through records or through persisted.head, so the text leaves room for the strict reading the blind agent raised. Reading persisted records only would change Example 2's golden output.
items.annex_wording: A.12.7.1 (add): "records may hold claim judgments signed by their judge or by a base-declared relay; they are validated (RJ01-RJ10, RJ12-RJ14) and evaluated exactly as the same statement in persisted.head would be. D28 concerns review lines only: a shape judge or shape reject line without a relay makes no judgment."

items.text: No value disagrees. Of the 43 distinct 16-hex values in spec/EXAMPLES.md, 42 appear in the goldens of the scenarios they describe. The 43rd, external_body 9dbce5edea4f3d2e, appears in none, which is correct: that clause raises nothing (A.14.2.6). Of A.14's 17 values, 032ab91f227efdd5 and ee776f8f2ec7de37 are the subject digests of the ex1-C-answered relay records and match. The others are input digests, or values no input carries: the non-representative call facts 2b03bf…/3aae2a…, the equivalence record b94ba363…/5f0d0c1e…, and the retired Hatch clause dc8454f2….

Example 3 Step 1 says one judge line 'makes the relay commit a judgment; the next run passes', but neither the Step 1 shape nor the v6 input declares a relay. Under D28 (A.7.6.8) that line would be unrecorded and the run would stay owed. The example text is right: A.11.5's acceptance test expects 'one persisted judgment, then pass'. So the input was changed to declare tooling::reviews and carry its claim judgment.

Example 1's base is syntax §1, whose fastCheck implementation binds pkgjson("package.json#scripts.test"). A.14.1.1 says the base package.json has no scripts, so that identity would not exist. The inputs keep v6's implementation paths. No output depends on this, because package.json and bun.lock never change, but the text should reconcile the two.

'Empty base: owed' (Example 1, and A.11.5 'empty base on syntax §1: owed') against the literal L7 rule in A.8.2.3. The head names a manifest identity that the empty base lacks. Read literally, 'undecided iff … the manifest identity changed' gives an undecided L7 on subject shape at critical, which DefaultPolicy blocks. The golden follows EXAMPLES and A.11.5, reading D18's 'skips what an empty base cannot say' as covering every field of the missing shape declaration. The normative L7 text exempts only owners and should say this.

Variant B: EXAMPLES says only 'authority a cause', and v6 printed 4 causes. A.14.1.3 lists 5, the last being 'AppendOnly (tier final; Lvl_b final at AuditStore.*)'. The golden follows A.14.1.3 and adds the forbid claim as the root cause.

Variant C prints the phase-1 line as 'shape approve bd:a7514dcb4cfb7068 bd:6bca5b3fe0d0787d', which is not codepoint order, while A.14.1.8 sorts about.refs. This is cosmetic: command is not core output, and the relayed records use the sorted order.

'After Step 2: a refactor of isoToday is covered by tsClockScan and raises no judgment obligation' is not exercised by any input. In the ex3-step2 inputs RefactorSensitive is still attached, so a refactor would stale ann's judgment and raise unestablished(stale), a judgment-class obligation. The sentence holds only if Step 2 includes the RefactorSensitive removal; the text should say so.
